clue.text: Taught us sound shell manoeuvres, it has!

indicators.note: sound tells the solver to say the words 'Taught us' out loud and hear a different word

parts.note: the two words, spoken, give the whole entry; the Mock Turtle in Alice says the schoolmaster was so called because he taught us

explanation.surface: A drill instructor boasts that his shell-formation training has been taught to the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the creature carries a shell about wherever it goes, and the Roman shield formation was named after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow reptile with a domed carapace carries its shell with it as it moves.

clue.text: Sport I organised to an honourable degree

indicators.note: organised means the letters of 'Sport I' are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims that playing games earned them a degree with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University's honours degree examinations are each called a Tripos, so this is a British academic term.
explanation.definitionFit: At Cambridge University the honours examination course is named this, after the three-legged stool once used there.

clue.text: Make good progress

explanation.surface: Advice to fix what is broken and get on with things.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the formal verb 'to repair to', meaning to go somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To mend is to make good; to betake oneself somewhere, an old formal verb sense, is to go or proceed.

clue.text: Gold lace for Iris

explanation.surface: A gift of golden lace intended for a woman called Iris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iris' looks like a woman's name but is the flower whose root yields orris powder.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an old embroidery of gold or silver thread and the iris plant used for perfume.

clue.text: Crate of cakes for the street corner orator?

definitions.text: Crate of cakes for the street corner orator?

parts.words: Crate of cakes for the street corner orator?
parts.note: a box that once held cakes of soap, stood on by a speaker in the street to address passers-by

explanation.surface: A speaker on a street corner stands on an old crate that once held cakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cakes' here are bars of soap, not baked goods; old wooden soap crates were the traditional platform for public speakers.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu public speakers once stood on wooden crates used to ship bars of washing product.

clue.text: Cluster round rally leader for a compromise meal

indicators.note: round means the cluster word goes around the other piece

parts.note: a cluster is a bunch

indicators.note: leader means take the first letter of the word rally

explanation.surface: Protesters gather round the leader of their rally for a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-morning meal is a compromise between breakfast and lunch.

clue.text: Feature Mark Antony's friendly countryman knows, he says

parts.note: Mark Antony's speech in Julius Caesar opens 'Friends, Romans, countrymen', so his countryman is a Roman

indicators.note: he says signals that the next word is spoken and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: the word knows, said out loud, sounds like the facial organ for smelling

explanation.surface: Something Mark Antony's countryman is said to know about.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'friendly countryman' is from Shakespeare's 'Friends, Romans, countrymen' speech; 'he says' turns 'knows' into a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooked, prominent nose with a high bridge is a facial feature.

clue.text: Peace, son, otherwise you're trapped!

indicators.note: otherwise means the letters of 'Peace, son' are put another way

explanation.surface: A parent tells a son to keep quiet or he will be stuck.
explanation.definitionFit: Being trapped means there is no way out to get away.

clue.text: Give the boss a break to ease his chairmanship

parts.note: the boss is the head of an organisation
a break is a rest

explanation.surface: Advice to give the chairman some time off so he can ease his duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chairmanship' is read as sitting in a chair: the cushion supports the sitter's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A support at the top of a seat back eases the neck of whoever sits in the chair.

clue.text: Where a veil is drawn over better halves and quarters

definitions.text: Where a veil is drawn over better halves and quarters

parts.words: Where a veil is drawn over better halves and quarters
parts.note: wives (better halves) and the women's quarters of a house kept screened from view in some South Asian custom

explanation.surface: A remark about drawing a discreet veil over certain matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better halves' are wives and 'quarters' are living rooms; purdah is the South Asian practice of secluding women behind curtains or veils.
explanation.definitionFit: Purdah is the custom of screening women from men's sight, so women there are kept in seclusion.

clue.text: Low creature with increasingly divisive ways

definitions.text: Low creature with increasingly divisive ways

parts.words: Low creature with increasingly divisive ways
parts.note: a simple single-celled organism that multiplies by splitting in two

explanation.surface: A description of a lowly person who keeps causing division.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divisive' sounds like a political insult, but this organism reproduces by dividing, so its numbers increase by division.
explanation.definitionFit: A single-celled protozoan, low on the scale of life, reproduces by binary fission.

clue.text: Handled fabric

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Handled fabric (4)' is a double definition giving FELT (touched; a cloth), but the held answer is PELT, which neither sense supports.

clue.text: Please teacher, I nearly bled! Can I be left out?

parts.note: a pupil's 'O, Miss!' calling for the teacher's attention

indicators.note: nearly means the word bled loses its final letter

parts.note: bled is taken whole before its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A schoolchild pleads with the teacher to be excused after a nosebleed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Please teacher' is the cry 'O, Miss!'; 'nearly' cuts the last letter off BLED to give BLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that may be left out is capable of being omitted.

clue.text: More pleasant resort having royal connection

parts.note: Nice is a resort on the French Riviera
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN for Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A holiday resort is more agreeable for having links with the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of an adjective meaning pleasant or agreeable.

clue.text: Fellow coming to vote for the cat

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a voter marks a cross, X, on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A man turns up to cast his vote for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: The breed is the tailless cat from the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: A breed of tailless cat from the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Gabriel may be spirited, but his port's often frozen

explanation.surface: The angel Gabriel is lively, though the harbour he gives his name to is icy.
explanation.walkthrough: The port, now Arkhangelsk in northern Russia, is on the White Sea and is ice-bound much of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabriel is a chief angel, a spirit; the Russian White Sea port of that English name is icebound in winter.

clue.text: Ring up in French very active companies performing

indicators.note: in means the ring and up pieces go inside the French word

parts.note: the French word for very is très
a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call in French to very lively performing companies.
explanation.definitionFit: Bands of travelling actors or dancers are companies that perform.

clue.text: Support the cause of the gold collector

explanation.surface: Backing a cause, like a winner collecting gold.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to back it; a winner of gold medals is the top competitor.

clue.text: Screwball with first-rate drug

parts.note: crack as an adjective means first-rate, as in crack troops
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An eccentric who takes top-quality drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or crazy person is a screwball.

clue.text: Chariot off course-the main one?

indicators.note: off course means the letters of the chariot word go astray into a new order

explanation.surface: A chariot that has strayed from its racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Course' sets up a racing chariot, but the definition is a meal course: a haricot is also a mutton stew served as a main course.
explanation.definitionFit: A haricot of mutton is a stew, served as the main course of a dinner.

clue.text: Record leading athlete broke

explanation.surface: The winning athlete set a record by breaking it.
explanation.walkthrough: The race winner breaks the finishing tape stretched across the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To record sound is to put it on magnetic strip; a winning runner breaks the strip at the finish.

clue.text: Head off 13: he'll finish off the gateau

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the referenced word is removed

parts.note: 13 points to the solution of clue 13-across, more pleasant

explanation.surface: A person who will finish off the cake.
explanation.walkthrough: The one finishing the gateau puts frosting on its top.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who applies frosting completes the decoration of a cake.

clue.text: Accuse little devil above everyone

indicators.note: above in a down clue places the first piece over the second

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
each means every one

explanation.surface: A mischievous child accuses everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a public official formally with misconduct is to accuse.

clue.text: Mad king goes back around church for her

indicators.note: around means the king piece encloses the church abbreviation
goes back means the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: King Lear goes mad in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A mad king heads back around a church to find a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's given name, so 'her' indicates a female person.

clue.text: Bad weeks never ending, keeping our joint together

indicators.note: bad means the letters of weeks are spoiled into a new order
ending means take the last letter of the word never

explanation.surface: Bad weeks that never end, while we keep our relationship together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' is a joint of meat held together on a spit or pin.
explanation.definitionFit: A pin through a roast or kebab holds the meat together while it cooks.

clue.text: Monday circle taking tea or coffee

parts.note: a circle is shaped like O
cha is a British colloquial word for tea

explanation.surface: On Monday the circle takes tea or coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine Arabian coffee, or a coffee drink flavoured with chocolate.

clue.text: It's bound to be not at all hard to read

definitions.text: It's bound to be not at all hard to read

parts.words: It's bound to be not at all hard to read
parts.note: a book with a soft cover, bound but not in hard boards, and an easy read

explanation.surface: A remark that something is bound to be easy reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' means fixed in covers, and 'not hard' means soft-covered rather than easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A book bound in soft card covers rather than stiff boards.

clue.text: Beam on to artificial silk

parts.note: a beam of light is a ray

explanation.surface: Light shining on to a man-made fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-made textile from cellulose, sold as imitation silk.

clue.text: Jim pugnaciously shows how to make a wordy attack

indicators.note: shows means the letters are on display inside the words Jim pugnaciously

explanation.surface: A man named Jim aggressively demonstrates how to attack someone with words.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or challenge something with argument is to attack it verbally.

clue.text: Very small exhibition? Could be a howling success!

explanation.surface: A tiny exhibition that turns out a roaring success.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the exhibition as one of tiny things; the second notes the infants on show cry a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A competition judging infants is a display of the very little; with crying entrants it is full of howls.

clue.text: Let 10 develop sting

indicators.note: develop means the letters of the two pieces grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: 10 is the number ten, spelt out

explanation.surface: Allowing ten to grow into a sting.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is read as the number ten, not a reference to another clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate or annoy someone is to sting them, and the stinging plant gives the verb.

clue.text: The general dealer who led ranch astray

indicators.note: astray means the letters of 'led ranch' wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A trader who led a ranch off course.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in general supplies, originally a maker and seller of candles.
